contradicting_evidence: Latest hourly BTC and ETH returns were positive, with taker-buy shares above half and falling OI, leaving stabilization or a rebound credible.
ETH's 24h loss was smaller than BTC's, while hourly ETH/BTC was flat; the current snapshot does not independently confirm renewed relative deterioration.
Only one settled ETF session is supplied, so persistent institutional outflows cannot be assumed.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: The balance favors renewed weakness or a rebound that fails to develop into sustained recovery. Broad-alt proxies remain vulnerable relative to BTC and ETH. This is a conditional downside bias, not a forecast of continuous selling or a precisely timed retest.
falsification_conditions: Sustained price advances accompanied by persistent spot buying, stronger ETH/BTC and broadening participation would invalidate the failed-rebound thesis.
Improving settled flows together with stabilizing liquidity and durable breadth recovery would materially weaken the downside bias.
missing_evidence: Repeated breadth observations establishing persistence rather than a single weak cross-section.
Newer settled ETF results and evidence of whether outflows continue or reverse.
Whether subsequent price gains occur with sustained spot demand rather than predominantly position reduction.
supporting_evidence: Current breadth shows 80 decliners against 19 advancers, with a negative median return and an equal-weight mean return near -1.80%.
Within that same breadth family, large-, mid- and small-alt proxies have advance ratios near 12%, 17% and 11%, and equal-weight losses around 2%; participation is broadly weak.
The latest final ETF session reported BTC outflows of $635.6 million and ETH outflows of $110.6 million.
